summary: Redwood-led SDK integration walkthrough focused on Python and TypeScript quickstarts, auth patterns (API key + environment variables), onboarding steps for a pilot, and security questions (SAML, KMS, SOC2). SE ran through sample code, console demo, and Optimize suggestions for batching/quantization. Customer requested sandbox creds, pricing, and a pilot kickoff.
topics:
1) Quickstart: pip/npm install, env var REDWOOD_API_KEY, basic request
2) Auth & roles: API keys vs. SSO, RBAC, KMS for secrets
3) Console walkthrough: routes, keys, quota, logs
4) Optimize: batching/caching suggestions, quantization profiles
5) Pilot scoping: success metrics, timeline, benchmarks
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone thanks for joining, we're gonna run through the SDK integration quickstart for Redwood, mostly Python and TypeScript examples, and then Priya will demo the console and optimize tooling.
[00:22] Michael: Great, thanks — we've got Sara and Devon here too, I'm Michael, CTO at Nova Retail, we're evaluating options for checkout fraud detection and product search reranking using embeddings.
[00:40] Jordan: Awesome. Quick q to start — current infra? are you leaning self-host or hosted?
[00:52] Sara: We're mostly cloud-native on GCP; we have some compliance needs, data residency in US and EU, and we'd probably want a VPC/private deployment eventually. Also interested in latency for short queries.
[01:14] Priya: Totally, and Redwood supports hosted for fast start, Dedicated for reserved GPU pools, and Private (VPC/on-prem). For pilot usually hosted or dedicated depending on traffic; we can scope private later.
[01:36] Devon: And auth — how do keys work with our SSO? We use Okta.
[01:44] Jordan: Good q; we support API keys for service-to-service. For enterprise we do SAML SSO + SCIM for user provisioning and RBAC in the console. You can bind API keys to roles and projects.
[02:05] Priya: I'll show the quickstart now. Python pip install is 'pip install redwood-inference' (note: sample package name may be slightly different depending on the release). Then set env var REDWOOD_API_KEY with your key. Example: export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_live_xxx.
[02:30] Priya: Code sample: from redwood import Client 
client = Client(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY'))
resp = client.text.generate(model='redwood-1', prompt='Summarize this...')
(there's small typos in the auto-transcript; actual repo has exact syntax).
[03:05] Sara: For TypeScript — is it npm install @redwood/inference?
[03:10] Priya: Yes, npm i @redwood/inference and then import Redwood from '@redwood/inference' const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY }) — request patterns are promise-based and support streaming in Node.
[03:40] Jordan: A note on envs: we recommend using secret manager + KMS/HSM to rotate keys. For private installs keys can be issued by your IAM and integrated with your KMS.
[04:05] Michael: Any rate limits on hosted? we have bursty traffic during promos.
[04:12] Priya: Hosted has default quotas, you can request increases. Dedicated gives predictable throughput and auto-scale policies with reserved capacity. For burst you can configure burst capacity or fallback to cheaper model variants.
[04:40] Devon: Ok show us the console?
[04:46] Priya: Switching over — console has API key management, per-route analytics, token cost breakdown, and rollout controls. Here's creating a key scoped to project 'nova-checkout' and role 'inference-runner'.
[05:20] Priya: You can pin model versions for rollouts, do canary deploys, and set automatic fallback to a lower-cost model if latency or capacity thresholds breach.
[05:45] Sara: How about observability for per-token costs? we need to show finance.
[05:50] Jordan: Console shows token counts and cost per route; Optimize can suggest batching/caching to reduce per-token unit cost. We'll share a sample cost spreadsheet.
[06:20] Priya: Now quick dive on Optimize — it analyzes request patterns, recommends continuous batching, KV prefix cache for repeated context, and quantization profiles for models where quality isn't heavily impacted.
[06:48] Michael: Can you run a bench on our p50/p95 latencies?
[06:54] Priya: For pilot we can run a bench using your sample payloads. We'll need a sandbox key, sample traces, and expected QPS. We'll run both hosted and dedicated sim to compare p50/p95 and cost.
[07:20] Devon: What's the SDK footprint and latency overhead? we've seen SDK wrappers add 30-50ms in some vendors.
[07:30] Priya: SDK is thin; most overhead is network. For Node/Python the client is lightweight. On dedicated instances you can get sub-30ms token generation for short sequences, but depends on model and sequence length.
[08:05] Sara: Any gotchas for streaming in TS?
[08:10] Priya: Streaming uses EventSource/ReadableStream; in Node we provide helpers. There's occasional mismatched content-length in proxies — so ensure your proxy supports chunked transfer.
[08:40] Jordan: Security questions — SOC 2, ISO?
[08:45] Priya: We are SOC 2 compliant and maintain audit logs; for private we can enable customer-managed logging retention and KMS for keys. We'll share the security pack (SOC2 report, pen test summary, network diagrams).
[09:05] Michael: Data residency — can we pin model serving to EU region?
[09:12] Priya: Yes, region routing is supported; you can create a region-specific pool or use private deployment in your VPC.
[09:28] Sara: About batching — if we batch user queries to amortize cost how does that affect latency?
[09:35] Priya: Batching trades throughput for latency. Optimize will recommend batching windows and thresholds; you can set per-route SLOs so latency-sensitive routes bypass batching.
[10:05] Jordan: Let's walk the developer quickstart for a simple embedding call — this is common for search rerank.
[10:14] Priya: Python example: client.embeddings.create(model='embed-small', input=['prod desc', 'user query'])
[10:26] Priya: Then upsert into vector DB; we have sample connectors in the repo. For TS similar pattern.
[10:45] Sara: Do you have connector examples for Pinecone/Weaviate?
[10:49] Priya: Yes, sample snippets for Pinecone/Weaviate/Postgres+pgvector in the examples folder.
[11:10] Michael: How do we handle PII? We need deterministic logging controls.
[11:16] Priya: You can disable recording for routes or redact at the SDK layer; also use KMS for key material and audit logs for access.
[11:30] Devon: Pricing — do you do per-token for hosted and flat for dedicated?
[11:34] Jordan: Hosted is per-token and embeddings per-unit; Dedicated is reserved capacity commit plus overage rules. We'll send you a pricing sheet.
[12:05] Priya: Ok demo time — here's a live snippet in TypeScript, quick run. (small audio gap, typing)
[12:30] [typing noise] Priya: Ok response came back, streaming worked, you can see cost and token counts in the console.
[12:55] Sara: Nice, sometimes model names get mangled in transcripts — what models are in the catalog?
[13:00] Jordan: We curate open models and Redwood-verified models. Model names like redwood-1, redwood-1-small, open-llama-v2 etc; we include performance profiles.
[13:25] Michael: For pilot we want to run a 2-week bench against paper-live traffic — can you outline success metrics?
[13:32] Jordan: Suggested metrics: p50/p95 latency for inference, cost per 1M tokens, accuracy/regression on a test set (specific to rerank), and error rate. We'll produce a bench checklist.
[14:00] Priya: Onboard timeline: set up sandbox creds (1 day), run bench (3-5 days), review results and plan dedicated/prod (1 week after).
[14:20] Devon: Access controls — can we restrict keys to IP ranges?
[14:25] Priya: Yes for Dedicated/private you can restrict via VPC and network ACLs; hosted keys support CIDR allowlists.
[14:48] Sara: Any known issues with GCP load balancers?
[14:53] Priya: Occasionally proxy buffering causes streaming hiccups; config to ensure chunked transfer works fixes it. We'll include troubleshooting notes.
[15:10] Michael: What's the expected work from our side for the pilot?
[15:15] Jordan: Provide sample payloads, QPS targets, acceptance test dataset, and point engineer for integration. We'll provide SDK examples, bench harness, and a walkthrough.
[15:40] Priya: One more note on quantization — for rerank where quality is sensitive we suggest int8-ish profiles and run evals to ensure no regressions. Optimize can flag quality drift.
[16:05] Sara: Who owns rollouts if models degrade? can we auto-fallback?
[16:10] Priya: Yes, you can configure automatic fallback to a pinned lower-cost model, and set thresholds for rollback. Rollouts are controlled in the console with canary percentages.
[16:40] Michael: Any compliance paperwork? NDA, DPA?
[16:45] Jordan: We'll send DPA and standard enterprise addenda; security pack has the items you need.
[17:05] Priya: Ok final checklist and next steps: Jordan will email pricing and pilot doc; I'll share sandbox key and bench sheet. Let's target pilot kickoff on 2026-12-08.
[17:30] Sara: Sounds good.
[17:35] Michael: Thanks folks.
[17:38] Jordan: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the artifacts.
[17:45] [call ends]
